key_insight: Machine-learning models can accurately predict band gaps in diverse halide perovskites using simple atomic and structural descriptors, revealing that B-site and X-site chemistry dominate the trend.
engineering_relevance: These predictions can speed up screening and design of low-toxicity perovskites for optoelectronic and solar-cell applications by reducing reliance on trial-and-error synthesis.
method: Trained ensemble tree models on atomic and structural features.
Compared random forest, GBRT, and XGB for band-gap prediction.
Used feature-importance analysis to identify the most influential descriptors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy across multiple halide-perovskite compositions, with feature-importance analysis used to validate the learned relationships.
watch_item: Model transferability may be limited if new perovskite chemistries fall outside the training composition space or if descriptor quality is inconsistent.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
